newsitem.title: ITALY: MOTOR RACING-SENNA DEATH TRIAL POSTPONED TO MAY.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SENNA DEATH TRIAL POSTPONED TO MAY.

text.p: The manslaughter trial over the race death in 1994 of Formula One driver Ayrton Senna has been postponed until May, a judge said on Monday.

Presiding judge Antonio Costanzo said the trial of six people, including Formula One team boss Frank Williams and technical director Patrick Head, would resume on May 6 when a revised calendar would also be drawn up.
Costanzo said the delay was due to the burden of other commitments, preventing him being in court.

Formula One boss Bernie Ecclestone had been scheduled to testify on April 24 before the weekend's San Marino Grand Prix at Imola while reigning world champion Damon Hill was due to appear in court the day after the race on April 28.
Senna died in a crash at the Imola track on May 1, 1994, when his Williams car careered off the track and crashed into a concrete wall at around 210 kph.
The prosecution alleges that a faulty weld on the steering column of Senna's car contributed to the death of the Brazilian three-times world champion.
The other accused are Williams former chief designer Adrian Newey, Belgian international race director Roland Bruynseraede and Imola officials Federico Bendinelli and Giorgio Poggi.
